title: Insurance Coverage for Machine Learning Startups and How It Is Provided
summary: The policies machine learning startups should review, how AI endorsements work, and what to prepare when comparing coverage through Corgi and other providers.
body_markdown:
### Tech E&O: when your product costs a customer money


[Technology Errors and Omissions insurance](https://www.corgi.insure/tech-eo) addresses covered claims that your technology products or services caused a customer financial loss. Think of an integration error or a faulty calculation a client relied on. It is different from coverage for damage to your own equipment or a breach of customer data.


For an ML business, ask whether the proposed policy addresses your model's actual use. A prediction that causes a customer loss, a discriminatory recommendation and a dispute over training data can raise different coverage questions. Don't assume that all three fall within a standard software policy.


### Cyber: when data or systems are compromised


[Cyber Liability](https://www.corgi.insure/cyber-liability) addresses covered security and privacy claims. For an ML company, that can matter when customer prompts, training datasets or other sensitive information are exposed.


Separate liability to other people from your own response costs. Corgi's published Cyber summary describes a third-party liability base form; breach response, ransomware and business interruption protections require the relevant endorsements. Review those components in your quote if your business needs them.


### D&O: when a claim concerns how the company was run


[Directors and Officers insurance](https://www.corgi.insure/directors-and-officers) focuses on covered management claims against company leaders. Investors or incoming board members may ask for it during a financing. It doesn't replace Tech E&O for a product-performance dispute.


### General Liability: when the risk is physical


[Commercial General Liability](https://www.corgi.insure/general-liability) addresses covered bodily injury, property damage and certain personal or advertising injury claims. A landlord or customer may require it. It isn't a substitute for insuring the financial harm your model could cause.


As you hire and grow, review


[EPLI](https://www.corgi.insure/blog/epli-insurance-for-startups) , Media Liability and


[Fiduciary Liability](https://www.corgi.insure/blog/fiduciary-liability-insurance-for-startups) where relevant. The trigger is a change in your operations, contracts or benefits—not just the label on your latest funding round.
